attributes.content: Mei-Lin Cho is an associate at Sullivan & Cromwell in the corporate group, having joined after clerking for a federal district judge in the Southern District of New York. She grew up in Flushing, Queens, and was introduced to the museum through the Young Patrons Circle by a law school classmate. Her collecting is at an early stage — she owns two photographs by contemporaries she met at an ICP open studio event — but she has a genuine and informed aesthetic curiosity and attends openings regularly. Mei-Lin runs the Prospect Park half marathon annually and trains with a running club that meets on Saturday mornings in Park Slope. She volunteers with a pro bono arts law clinic that assists emerging artists with contract and intellectual property questions. Priya Mehta manages the relationship and notes she is thoughtful, slightly reserved in group settings, and responds best to small-group cultivation events. Annual gift of $2,500. Recommend inviting her to the Young Patrons advisory committee to deepen engagement and accelerate relationship development.

Rosemary Cavendish is a private wealth advisor at a boutique family office serving ultra-high-net-worth clients in New York and London. She spent fifteen years at Goldman Sachs's private wealth management division before joining her current firm as a managing partner. Rosemary and her husband Geoffrey, a retired art dealer, live in a large apartment on the Upper East Side and have a weekend house in Litchfield, Connecticut. Their collection, guided by Geoffrey's expertise, is significant: it includes works by Color Field painters, mid-century photographs, and several major Abstract Expressionist works on paper. Rosemary sits on the museum's finance committee and serves on the advisory board of the Dia Art Foundation. Geoffrey has been a quiet advisor to the museum's acquisitions committee and participates in dealer advisory conversations. James Reuter manages the primary relationship with Rosemary. The family does not have a foundation but gives through a substantial donor-advised fund. Major gift potential; the director should attend the next lunch scheduled with Geoffrey.

metadata.name: Rosemary Cavendish
metadata.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Kwame Asante is a cardiologist and professor of medicine at Weill Cornell Medical College, where he also directs a research lab focused on cardiac imaging. He grew up in the Bronx and did his undergraduate work at Howard University before medical school at Columbia. Kwame and his wife Ama live in Park Slope with their daughter, who attends Brooklyn Friends School. He is passionate about art as a form of resistance and narrative, and his collecting interests center on Basquiat-era Neo-Expressionism and Kerry James Marshall's figurative work. He owns two Marshall prints acquired through the Studio Museum's benefit auction and has attended every Studio Museum benefit for the past eight years. He is also a board member of the Studio Museum in Harlem. Kwame attended Art Basel Miami Beach in 2024 for the first time and connected with our development associate there. He supports several arts organizations through a donor-advised fund at the New York Community Trust. He runs — completed the Chicago Marathon in October 2024, his fifth marathon — and coaches a youth running program in Brownsville. Diana Flores manages this relationship. Potential to grow from annual to mid-tier with focused cultivation.

Richard Baxter-Oduya is a managing director at a large family office, the Horton Family Office, managing a $4 billion portfolio across public and private assets for a single family. He joined after eight years at BlackRock's multi-asset strategies group. Richard lives in a townhouse in the East Eighties with his wife Ngozi, a secondary school principal, and their two children. He has been a mid-level museum donor for four years and is on a clear trajectory toward major donor status. His collecting interests are in Abstract Expressionism, particularly Franz Kline and de Kooning; he made his first significant purchase — a de Kooning lithograph — at a Sotheby's sale in 2023 and has been actively building his knowledge since. He attended Art Basel Miami Beach in December 2024 for the first time and spent time with our staff at the VIP preview. Richard is a competitive offshore sailor — his 46-foot Baltic sloop, Hazel Run, completed the Newport-Bermuda race in June 2024. He also plays squash competitively at the Racquet and Tennis Club. James Reuter manages this relationship. Next step: an invitation to join the acquisitions committee would align with his interests and deepen institutional commitment.

metadata.name: Richard Baxter-Oduya
metadata.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Peter Kessler is a retired hedge fund manager who ran a market-neutral equity fund, Kessler Capital Management, for seventeen years before closing it in 2020 to manage his personal assets. He and his wife Ellen live in a duplex penthouse on the Upper West Side and have a summer home in Edgartown, Martha's Vineyard. Peter has been a major donor since 2015 and is a member of the director's leadership circle. His collecting interests are broad and eclectic — he has significant holdings in Abstract Expressionism, particularly Rothko and Pollock, as well as important contemporary photography including a large Gursky print purchased at Phillips in 2018. He attended Art Basel Basel annually for twelve years and has strong relationships with several major galleries. The Kessler Family Foundation supports the museum, the Whitney Museum Council, and Jazz at Lincoln Center. He plays competitive tennis at the USTA 4.5 level through his New York Athletic Club and has competed in club tournaments nationally. James Reuter manages this relationship in close coordination with the president. A campaign gift at the $2.5 million level is under active discussion. Kessler has expressed mild frustration with the pace of the museum's building renovation — this concern should be addressed proactively.

metadata.name: Peter Kessler
metadata.location: Upper West Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Priscilla Ng is co-founder and CEO of a Series B SaaS company serving the architecture and engineering sectors, based in DUMBO. She launched the company in 2018 after a decade in product management at Autodesk and Bentley Systems. Priscilla lives in DUMBO and is deeply embedded in the Brooklyn tech and arts communities — she serves on the board of the Public Art Fund, attending monthly meetings in their Chelsea offices. Her collecting is focused on Minimalism: she has acquired works by Anne Truitt and Robert Irwin through gallery relationships developed over four years of attending art fairs, most recently Art Basel Miami and Frieze New York. She attended the museum's architecture and art symposium in April and met the director for the first time, expressing interest in the planned outdoor sculpture installation. Priya Mehta should schedule a follow-up to discuss an annual-to-mid upgrade and potential multi-year commitment tied to the public art programming budget.

Nora Callahan is a managing director at a long/short equity hedge fund based in Midtown, specializing in technology sector analysis. She was previously at Goldman Sachs in the equities division for seven years before moving to the buy side. Nora lives on the Upper West Side with her husband and two college-age children. She is a competitive sailor: she co-owns a Swan 48 named Silverline and competed in the Newport-Bermuda race in June, finishing fourth in her class. Sailing has connected her to a network of financially prominent collectors, several of whom she has introduced to the museum. Nora's collecting focus is Abstract Expressionism — she owns two Rothko works on paper and a de Kooning oil she acquired at Christie's in 2017. She attended Art Basel Basel last June, combining it with a European sailing trip. James Reuter manages the relationship and should propose naming the Abstract Expressionism study room at the $150,000 level — she has signaled readiness for a meaningful upgrade from her current mid-tier giving.

metadata.name: Nora Callahan
metadata.location: Upper West Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Sunita Varma is a managing director at JPMorgan Chase's investment bank, leading the technology sector M&A team. She started her career at Goldman Sachs in the TMT group before moving to JPMorgan twelve years ago. She lives on the Upper East Side with her husband Rohit and their two children. Sunita has been interested in contemporary photography since her college years and has built a focused collection around Cindy Sherman — she owns four works from different phases of Sherman's career and recently added a piece from the Society Portraits series through a New York gallery. She attended Art Basel Miami for the third time in December and describes the fair as the one annual event she would sacrifice almost any other commitment to attend. She is a member of the Whitney Museum Council and attends their programming regularly alongside her museum involvement. Sarah Okafor manages the relationship; Sunita gives at the mid-tier level. Proposed next step: introduce her to the director over a private lunch and discuss a potential major gift toward the photography endowment.

metadata.name: Sunita Varma
metadata.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Tariq Al-Rashid is a managing director at BlackRock's multi-asset strategies group, where he oversees a team of portfolio managers focused on sovereign wealth clients in the Gulf and Southeast Asia. Before BlackRock he spent eight years at Barclays Capital in London and Dubai. He relocated to Tribeca four years ago with his wife Nadia and their two children, and they have become active supporters of several cultural institutions. Tariq collects contemporary photography — he has works by Taryn Simon and Richard Avedon's late commercial photography series — and recently loaned a Simon piece to a group show at ICP, on whose Photography Council he now sits. He attended Art Basel Miami Beach last December and met with the museum's director at a collector's dinner there. His motivations for giving are tied closely to education access: he has spoken repeatedly about wanting his children to see art by people who look like them. Next steps: Michael Torres to propose a co-branded education fund naming opportunity. Potential ask: $75,000 over three years.

Rafael Montoya is a senior associate at McKinsey & Company in the New York office, working primarily in the financial services practice. He graduated from MIT with a degree in electrical engineering before earning an MBA at Harvard, where he developed an interest in the economics of cultural institutions. Rafael has been a museum member for three years and upgraded to the Young Patrons Circle last winter. He collects contemporary photography, focusing on Latin American artists — he owns prints by Graciela Iturbide and recently acquired a piece by Pilar Wiley at the Untitled Art Fair. He attended the museum's Photography and the Archive symposium and followed up with a thoughtful email to curator Elliot Huang about a comparison he noticed between two pieces. Sarah Okafor is cultivating him for a move to mid-level giving; she believes a restricted gift toward the photography acquisition fund is achievable within the year. He is also a recreational soccer player competing in a NYCFC-affiliated adult league on weekends.

Richard Kazlauskas is a Goldman Sachs managing director in the private wealth management division, serving ultra-high-net-worth families. He grew up in Lithuania before emigrating to the United States at fifteen, eventually earning a degree in economics at Boston College and an MBA at Wharton. Richard lives in Tribeca with his partner and is an avid collector of Eastern European contemporary art — he owns works by Jarosław Kozłowski and significant Baltic photography from the 1980s. He attended Art Basel Miami Beach for five consecutive years and has begun attending Art Basel Basel as well. He sits on the advisory board of the International Center of Photography and has been instrumental in introducing several Eastern European collectors to the ICP community. James Reuter manages the museum relationship and has noted his interest in supporting a dedicated exhibition of Soviet-era photography. Next steps: circulate a concept proposal and set a meeting with the photography curator. Giving potential assessed at $50,000–$75,000 for a restricted exhibition gift.

Victoria Huang is a managing director at Lazard's restructuring advisory group, where she has worked for sixteen years following stints at Merrill Lynch and a boutique restructuring firm. She holds an undergraduate degree from Dartmouth and a JD/MBA joint degree from NYU. Victoria lives in the West Village with her husband and twin sons and has been a museum supporter for nine years. Her collecting interest centers on contemporary Chinese American artists — she owns significant works by Hung Liu and Martin Wong, and has been following the career of Wangechi Mutu's generation of artists closely. She attended Art Basel Hong Kong twice as a collector and is a member of the advisory board for Asian Arts at the Brooklyn Museum. Diana Flores manages the relationship and is cultivating a major gift conversation tied to a proposed exhibition on Chinese American artistic identity in New York. Victoria expressed strong enthusiasm at a recent cultivation dinner.

George Tanner is a managing director at Vanguard's institutional advisory business, working with large endowments and foundations. He has spent his entire career at Vanguard, joining from Princeton where he studied economics. He lives in Gladwyne, Pennsylvania, and commutes to New York three days a week, staying at a Midtown corporate apartment. He is a lifelong collector of Abstract Expressionism — he describes his collection as focused on 'the generation after the giants,' centering on work by second-wave de Kooning followers and Lee Krasner. He attended the museum's Abstract Expressionism study day and the associated evening dinner, where he sat next to a trustee who encouraged him to formalize his museum relationship. He skis in Vail every Presidents' Day week with college friends. He runs the Philadelphia Marathon each November. Relationship manager note: James Reuter manages this relationship. George is quietly generous and does not seek recognition. He gives $15,000 annually. An upgrade conversation toward $35,000 or a chair of the painting acquisitions committee is timely.

Rachel Bloom-Finkelstein is a partner at Sullivan & Cromwell in the private equity and M&A practice. She joined S&C directly from Columbia Law eighteen years ago and has been a partner for six years. She lives on the Upper West Side with her husband and twin sons. She collects Minimalism — she owns three Donald Judd stacks acquired over a decade and a Robert Irwin scrim installation currently on loan to a museum in Connecticut. She attended the museum's Minimalism symposium and the Judd Foundation benefit gala in the same season. She is on the board of the Dia Art Foundation and chairs their development committee. She skis in Aspen every spring break with her family, staying at a house they co-own with another family. Relationship manager note: Priya Mehta manages this relationship. Rachel gives $50,000 annually, primarily to Dia Art Foundation, with $15,000 to this museum. An upgrade conversation emphasizing the Minimalism collection synergy is appropriate. Target $40,000 for next year's ask.

metadata.name: Rachel Bloom-Finkelstein
metadata.location: Upper West Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Alexandra Petrov is a managing director at a Midtown hedge fund, Cormorant Capital, where she leads a long/short equities strategy focused on consumer and retail sectors. She is 41, Russian-born and a US citizen, and lives in a Park Avenue co-op she purchased six years ago. Her collecting focus is on contemporary photography — she is one of the more serious collectors of Cindy Sherman in her cohort, owning seven works across multiple series, and she has a strong interest in Nan Goldin's diary-format work. She attended Art Basel Basel and Frieze London in the same year and maintains relationships with gallerists in both cities. She is an accomplished alpine skier who spends two weeks in Verbier every January and has participated in charity slalom events there. Diana Flores manages the relationship. She has expressed interest in joining the museum's photography advisory group, and this should be formalized. Current mid-level giving at $22,000; step-up to $40,000 is realistic once committee engagement is established.

metadata.name: Alexandra Petrov
metadata.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Priscilla Nwosu is a 41-year-old management consultant and partner at Bain & Company's New York office, where she leads the media and entertainment practice. Originally from Lagos and raised partly in London, she has been based in New York for twelve years. She lives in the West Village with her husband, a documentary photographer whose work has appeared in the New Yorker. Her collecting interests are in contemporary photography — she owns prints by Richard Avedon and Cindy Sherman and recently commissioned a piece from an emerging Nigerian photographer through a Lagos gallery. She attended Frieze London last October and Frieze New York in May. Priscilla serves on the advisory board of Creative Time and is a member of the museum's director's circle. Diana Flores manages the relationship; Priscilla has been responsive and engaged, attending several curator-led tours. A $20,000–$25,000 ask for the contemporary photography acquisitions fund is planned for the fall solicitation. She has mentioned her interest in supporting programming that amplifies African and diaspora perspectives in contemporary photography — this should be incorporated into any proposal narrative. Her husband's photography connections may also be a cultivation avenue worth exploring.

Winston Akpan is a 49-year-old private equity partner at Apollo Global Management, where he focuses on consumer and media sector buyouts. Originally from Abuja and educated at Oxford and Harvard Business School, he has been in New York for fifteen years and lives in a townhouse in Brooklyn Heights. His wife, a corporate attorney at Sullivan & Cromwell, is also a museum donor. Winston's collecting interests center on Abstract Expressionism and West African contemporary art — he owns a Pollock work on paper, a Motherwell small canvas, and several works by contemporary Nigerian artists including Njideka Akunyili Crosby. He attended Art Basel Basel in June and Art Basel Miami in December. He serves as a trustee of the Studio Museum in Harlem, a role he has held for four years. His giving to this museum is at the mid tier; Priya Mehta manages the relationship. The household's combined philanthropic capacity is significant, and the museum should consider approaching the couple jointly. A $50,000 ask for the African diaspora contemporary art initiative is appropriate for this cycle. Winston is highly responsive to peer cultivation — a dinner with two other trustees from comparable institutions would be effective. Note that his wife's Sullivan & Cromwell connection overlaps with another donor in the portfolio.

Fatima Al-Rashid is a 53-year-old investment banker and managing director at Lazard's Middle East and North Africa advisory group, based in New York and traveling frequently to Riyadh and Abu Dhabi. Born in Beirut and educated at the American University of Beirut and Wharton, she has been based in New York for twenty years. She lives on the Upper East Side. Fatima's collecting interest is in contemporary Arab and Middle Eastern art — she owns works by Etel Adnan, Mona Hatoum, and Kader Attia, and has been a consistent attendee at Art Dubai and Art Basel Basel. She is a trustee of the Guggenheim Foundation's international affairs committee, through which she was introduced to this museum's director two years ago. Diana Flores manages the relationship. Fatima's philanthropic giving is channeled primarily through her family's Al-Rashid Cultural Fund, which supports cross-cultural arts programming globally. A conversation about a $75,000 co-sponsorship of the museum's upcoming program on contemporary art from the Arab world is planned for the spring. She is engaged and responsive but travels extensively; communications should be coordinated around her New York calendar windows, which are typically three or four days a month.

metadata.name: Fatima Al-Rashid
metadata.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: George Ellsworth is a 62-year-old portfolio manager at BlackRock's fundamental equities division, where he has worked for sixteen years after an earlier career at Fidelity Investments and a stint at a small value-focused boutique he co-founded in the early 2000s. He lives in Scarsdale with his wife Barbara, who is a landscape architect. George's museum connection came through a colleague who sits on the director's circle; he has given at the mid tier for six years. His collecting interests are in postwar American abstraction — he owns a Franz Kline oil on canvas, a Clyfford Still lithograph, and has been interested in adding a Lee Krasner to the collection. He attended Art Basel Basel last summer and the fall gala. Barbara has a stronger aesthetic sensibility and is often the more active museum participant; she attended a garden design and landscape art lecture at the museum last spring. Sarah Okafor manages the relationship and has built good rapport with both George and Barbara. A $35,000 ask for the abstract expressionism acquisitions fund is planned for this cycle. George runs the Boston Marathon most years — completed it last April — and is also an avid fisherman who spends summers on the Cape.

Sophia Andreou is a 56-year-old senior partner at Sullivan & Cromwell, where she specializes in securities regulation and financial institution compliance. Born in Athens and educated at the University of Athens Law School and Yale Law School, she has been a New York attorney for over twenty-five years. She lives in a pre-war apartment on the Upper East Side. Sophia's collecting interest is in classical and contemporary Greek sculpture and photography — she owns pieces by Greek photographers including Nikos Economopoulos and has been interested in how museums contextualize Mediterranean heritage alongside contemporary work. She is a museum donor at the mid tier, introduced to the institution three years ago through the museum's Hellenic arts advisory group. Diana Flores manages the relationship. Sophia also sits on the board of the New York Philharmonic in a governance capacity. She is a precise, analytical personality who responds well to program impact data and governance transparency in donor communications. A $25,000 ask for the international photography acquisitions fund is planned. She attended Art Basel Basel last June and has mentioned Frieze London as an annual fixture. Her Sullivan & Cromwell connection overlaps with a partner at another firm whose spouse is also a museum donor — worth noting for cross-referencing.

metadata.name: Sophia Andreou
metadata.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Jacques Moreau is a 58-year-old French-born commercial real estate financier and managing director at Natixis Real Estate Capital in New York, with a career history spanning BNP Paribas in Paris, Deutsche Bank in London, and his current role. He lives in a large apartment in the West Village with his wife Isabelle, who is a French language teacher at a private school. His collecting interests are in French and American postwar painting — he owns a Nicolas de Staël oil study, a Sam Francis watercolor, and has recently acquired a Franz Kline work on paper, drawn in by a conversation with the museum's postwar curator at a private dinner. He attended Art Basel Basel every year for the last twelve years and Frieze London in October. His museum giving is at the mid tier; Sarah Okafor manages the relationship, which deepened after the private dinner last fall. He is engaged and generous with his time — he hosted a small collector gathering at his apartment to benefit the museum's acquisitions fund. His wife Isabelle is interested in education programs. A $40,000 ask for the postwar European and American painting acquisitions fund is planned for the spring campaign. He is a competitive offshore sailor and raced the Fastnet race last year on his Oyster 54, Île de Ré.

Nicholas Papadopoulos is a 61-year-old senior managing director in Goldman Sachs's private wealth management division, where he has worked for twenty-two years after an earlier stint at Merrill Lynch. Greek-American, he grew up in Astoria and has maintained strong ties to the Queens Greek community throughout his career. He lives in a large apartment on Park Avenue. Nicholas's collecting focus is on abstract and figurative work by Greek and Greek-American artists — he owns several works by Jannis Kounellis and Lucas Samaras, as well as a Lucian Freud etching. He has also developed an interest in Abstract Expressionism and owns a Franz Kline drawing that he acquired from a colleague's estate. He attended Art Basel Basel for the past eight years. Diana Flores manages the relationship; Nicholas has been a mid-tier donor for six years and has responded warmly to collector dinners and private curator events. He is also a competitive offshore sailor: he raced the Sydney-Hobart race last December on a friend's Baltic 45, Κυανή Βαρεία, placing mid-fleet in his division. A $45,000 ask for the contemporary art acquisitions endowment is planned for the spring solicitation. His wife Maria is a board member at the Onassis Foundation, a connection worth exploring for programmatic collaboration.

metadata.name: Nicholas Papadopoulos
metadata.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Ifeoma Chukwuemeka is a 40-year-old senior associate at Weil, Gotshal & Manges, specializing in private equity fund formation and investment management regulation. Born in Onitsha, Nigeria, and raised in London, she attended Queen Mary University of London and Columbia Law School. She has been in New York for eight years and lives in Fort Greene, Brooklyn. Ifeoma's museum engagement began through a professional women's network that organized a members preview event at the museum two years ago. Her collecting interests are in contemporary African photography — she owns prints by Zanele Muholi and Malick Sidibé, and follows the work of Seun Akisanmi closely. She attended Frieze London last October while visiting family. Michael Torres manages the relationship. She is an annual-level donor and has been responsive and engaged; attending four or five programs per year. Her Weil Gotshal connection overlaps with the estate attorney mentioned for another major donor in the portfolio — an interesting coincidence that should not affect their separate relationship management. A mid-tier cultivation conversation is appropriate in the next twelve months, with the African photography acquisitions fund as the natural focus. She is also a USTA tennis player — competes in a doubles league in Brooklyn on weekends.

Camille Beaumont-Girard is a senior partner at Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom, specializing in mergers and acquisitions with a particular focus on cross-border European transactions. She trained at Sciences Po and Columbia Law and has been at Skadden for sixteen years. Camille lives in a townhouse in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, and is deeply embedded in the Brooklyn arts community — she serves on the acquisitions committee at the Brooklyn Museum. Her collecting interests center on contemporary photography; she owns prints by Cindy Sherman and Nan Goldin and attended Frieze New York last spring, where she was introduced to the museum's chief curator. She's a regular at the museum's members-only preview events and particularly enjoyed last year's talk on feminist photography. Her philanthropic giving is primarily directed through a donor-advised fund at Fidelity. Cultivation note: Camille has expressed interest in co-sponsoring a photography-focused catalogue. Next step is a lunch with James Reuter and the curator of photography in Q2. Potential ask of $35,000.

Catherine Drummond is a 65-year-old principal and founder of Drummond & Associates, a management consulting boutique serving nonprofit and philanthropic organizations. She spent the first half of her career at McKinsey & Company, where she was a partner in the social sector practice. She lives in a large apartment in Brooklyn Heights with her husband, a retired federal judge. Catherine is a sophisticated arts philanthropist — she serves on the board of the Guggenheim Foundation and has been a museum major donor for seven years. Her collecting interests center on Abstract Expressionism and she has a deep knowledge of the movement; she owns works by Motherwell and Franz Kline and has lent one piece to the museum. She attended Art Basel Basel as part of the museum's VIP group last June and also attended Frieze New York. The Drummond Foundation distributes approximately $600,000 annually, with arts and education as primary areas. Cultivation note: stewardship focus. Sarah Okafor to plan a private dinner with the director in Q1 to discuss a potential capital campaign gift.

Vikram Nair is a 48-year-old partner at Sullivan & Cromwell in the capital markets practice, having spent his entire career at the firm after graduating from Harvard Law. He lives with his family in Scarsdale, Westchester County, and commutes to the Midtown office. Vikram and his wife Ananya are co-founders of the Nair Family Foundation, which focuses on arts education and access, distributing around $250,000 per year. His collecting interests are in contemporary photography — he has built a careful collection of Andreas Gursky prints and follows the work of Cindy Sherman. He attended Art Basel Miami Beach last December and is a regular at Frieze New York. Vikram also sits on the advisory board of the ICP. He has given at the mid level to this museum for four years and attended a curator-led talk on photography last spring, which he described as one of the best museum events he's attended. Cultivation note: strong alignment with photography programming. Priya Mehta to explore a $50,000 endowed fund for photography education programming.

Elena Sorokina is a 59-year-old managing director at Lazard Asset Management, where she heads the fixed income quantitative strategies group. She began her career at Vanguard in Philadelphia and joined Lazard after completing an MBA at Chicago Booth. She lives in a large apartment in Midtown East. Elena's collecting interests center on contemporary photography — she has built a serious collection focused on Andreas Gursky and has recently acquired a work by Richard Avedon from an estate sale. She attended Frieze London last October and Art Basel Basel in June. Elena serves on the board of the New York Philharmonic and gives through a donor-advised fund. She has been giving at the mid level here for three years. She is an avid triathlete and completed Ironman Kona last October, finishing in the top quarter of her age group — a remarkable achievement at her age. Cultivation note: very driven personality; responds to excellence and prestige. James Reuter to propose a recognition event and explore a mid-to-major upgrade conversation around the music and sound art programming.

James Osei-Bonsu is a 55-year-old managing director in Goldman Sachs's private wealth management division, where he advises ultra-high-net-worth families on multi-generational wealth planning. He joined Goldman from Morgan Stanley twenty years ago. He lives in a townhouse in the West Village with his husband, an architect. James is a sophisticated and long-tenured museum donor who upgraded to major giving three years ago. His collecting interests span Abstract Expressionism and contemporary West African art — he owns a significant work by Clyfford Still and has been building a collection of Ghanaian and Nigerian contemporary artists. He attended Art Basel Basel and Art Basel Miami Beach in the same year for the first time last cycle. James is a board member of the Dia Art Foundation and gives through the Osei-Bonsu Family Foundation, which he and his husband established five years ago. Cultivation note: key relationship — significant additional gift potential. Sarah Okafor to schedule a quarterly check-in and discuss a five-year pledging commitment.

Elliot Varga is a managing director in Goldman Sachs's equity research division, covering large-cap consumer and retail. He has been at Goldman for eighteen years, having started as an analyst after graduating from Dartmouth. He and his wife Simone live in a pre-war co-op on the Upper West Side and spend summers in Watch Hill, Rhode Island. Elliot is a competitive offshore sailor who races a Swan 48 named Argent Rule; he has completed two Newport-Bermuda races and hopes to enter the Fastnet race in 2026. His collecting interests lean toward Abstract Expressionism — he recently purchased a Franz Kline ink study at Christie's and is actively looking for de Kooning works on paper. He attended the museum's Fall Preview evening in October 2024 and stayed late for the panel discussion on mid-century American painting. His assistant coordinates his calendar; any event invitations should come four to six weeks in advance. Sarah Okafor manages the relationship. Initial ask of $25,000 toward the permanent collection fund is appropriate.

metadata.name: Elliot Varga
metadata.location: Upper West Side, New York, NY

attributes.content: Carlos Mendes-Ribeiro is a managing director at a São Paulo-based asset manager, Meridiano Gestão, with a satellite office in New York that he runs. Brazilian-born, he attended Insper in São Paulo and received an MBA from Chicago Booth. He lives in a rented apartment in the East 50s while his family remains in São Paulo; he spends roughly three weeks a month in New York. His collecting interests are primarily Brazilian modernism and contemporary Latin American work, but he has recently developed a strong interest in Basquiat and the New York scene of the 1980s, which he encountered through a friend who is a film producer. He attended Art Basel Miami in 2024 for the first time. Michael Torres manages the relationship. He gave $5,000 in 2024. He has expressed enthusiasm about the museum as an ambassador for Brazilian collectors in New York. A joint cultivation strategy involving other Latin American donors and focused on the 1980s downtown New York scene would be compelling for him.

Andre Beaumont is a food and beverage entrepreneur who founded and sold two restaurant groups in New York before launching Beaumont Hospitality, a boutique hotel consultancy. He lives in a landmarked brownstone in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, that he has meticulously restored. His aesthetic sensibility informs his collecting: he favors figurative painting with psychological depth — he owns a Jenny Saville limited edition print and an Alice Neel portrait of an unknown subject acquired at auction in 2022. He attended Frieze New York in 2023 and 2024. Andre is a club-level tennis player who competes at the Brooklyn Bridge Park courts in a USTA league on summer weekday evenings. He gives $4,500 annually. Diana Flores manages the relationship. He has a wide network in the Brooklyn arts and hospitality community and has volunteered to host a small cultivation dinner for the museum at his home. This offer should be acted upon in spring 2025. An ask of $10,000–$15,000 following the dinner event is a reasonable next step.

Philip Oduya is a senior associate at Goldman Sachs's private wealth management division, working with ultra-high-net-worth families in the Northeast. Nigerian-British, he grew up in Lagos and London and came to New York for his MBA at Columbia. He lives in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, and is 31. He is an early-career donor — he gave $1,000 to the Annual Fund in 2024, his first gift. His collecting interest is nascent: he attended the Basquiat section of a museum group exhibition in February 2024 and stayed for ninety minutes, an unusually long dwell time noted by gallery staff. He is also interested in contemporary African photography after visiting a show at a Chelsea gallery with a colleague. He ran the NYC Marathon in 2023. Michael Torres manages the relationship. He has significant long-term potential through career trajectory and his employer's art advisory services. Cultivation should be peer-oriented: Young Collectors events and studio visits. No sensitivities noted.

Kwame Asante-Brown is a Chicago-based venture capitalist, a partner at Midway Ventures focused on climate technology. Ghanaian-American, he grew up on the South Side of Chicago and attended Northwestern for his undergraduate degree and MIT for his MBA. He maintains a close relationship with New York's art world through his sister, a gallery director in Chelsea, who first introduced him to the museum. He collects Neo-Expressionism with particular focus on Kerry James Marshall and Keith Haring: he owns two Marshall prints and an early Haring tarp painting acquired through the Estate. He attended Art Basel Miami in 2022 and 2024. He has given $5,000 in each of the last two years. Diana Flores manages the relationship. Despite his Chicago base, he visits New York five to seven times per year and has attended three museum events in 2024. His long-term giving potential is high given his career. A mid-tier cultivation path is appropriate; the next ask should be $12,000–$15,000.

Tariq Al-Rashid is a managing partner at a real estate private equity firm, Crescent Bridge Capital, which he co-founded in 2011 after leaving a VP role at Cushman & Wakefield. The firm focuses on mixed-use development in secondary markets — Pittsburgh, Nashville, and Detroit. He is 47, lives in the West Village, and travels extensively for deal flow. Tariq became a museum donor through his architect partner, whose firm designed a museum expansion in another city. His collecting interests span figurative painting and works on paper — he has pieces by Eric Fischl and a strong Nicole Eisenman oil acquired at Frieze New York in 2022. He also attended Art Basel Miami last December and purchased a work by a Berlin-based painter through a gallery introduction arranged by the museum's curatorial team. Michael Torres manages the relationship and hosted Tariq and his partner at a small curatorial dinner last spring. A mid-level ask of $30,000 for the education wing is planned for Q4. Tariq is private and does not want his name in public donor lists without prior discussion.

Sophia Andreou is a 43-year-old fashion designer and founder of a luxury ready-to-wear label, Andreou Studio, sold through Net-a-Porter and a flagship in SoHo. Born in Athens, she studied at Central Saint Martins and spent years at Dior before launching independently in 2014. She lives in Tribeca in a loft that doubles as a studio. Sophia has been a mid-tier museum donor for four years, drawn in by a crossover exhibition on fashion and photography that featured archival Avedon images. Her collection is photography-first: she has three Richard Avedon large-format portraits and recently acquired an Andreas Gursky image of a fashion show floor — she described it as almost diagnostic of her industry. She attended Frieze London last October and Frieze New York in May. Michael Torres manages the museum relationship. Sophia serves on the advisory board of the International Center of Photography and has introduced three colleagues as museum members. She is interested in sponsoring a fashion photography program and has given verbal encouragement to a $35,000 co-presenting proposal. Detailed proposal to follow from the development office in Q3. She prefers WhatsApp for scheduling.

David Park is a 47-year-old managing partner at a New York-based private equity firm, Keystone Growth Partners, which focuses on consumer and retail buyouts. He was born in Seoul, raised in Los Angeles, and attended UCLA for economics before earning his MBA at Columbia Business School. He has lived in the West Village for twelve years. David became a museum donor after attending Art Basel Miami for the first time in 2016 with a board member friend. He has attended every year since. His collecting interests span contemporary photography and Abstract Expressionism — he has a large-format Andreas Gursky print and two Clyfford Still lithographs acquired through a trusted gallery. He attended Frieze New York in May and had a curator walkthrough with the photography team. Priya Mehta manages the museum relationship. David is a mid-tier donor with major-tier capacity — he has been in a long cultivation cycle that the development team believes is close to a commitment. His wife, Christine, is less engaged with the museum but attended last year's gala and responded warmly to the curator. A dual invitation to a small private dinner is recommended as the next step. Potential ask: $75,000 for the photography acquisition fund. He races a 40-foot X-yacht named Headway in the Buzzards Bay Regatta each summer.

Raj Subramaniam is a managing director at BlackRock in their multi-asset strategies group, having joined from Goldman Sachs asset management eight years ago. He lives on the Upper West Side with his wife Meera, a pediatric cardiologist at Columbia Presbyterian. They have two teenage daughters. Raj's collecting interest has evolved significantly over the past decade: he began with South Asian modernists and has moved toward Minimalism, acquiring works by Donald Judd and Anne Truitt. He attended Art Basel Miami last December and came away with a large-format photograph by Andreas Gursky. He joined the museum's Contemporaries giving circle two years ago and has attended four of the six annual events since. He and Meera attended the museum's Minimalism study day last March and he spoke enthusiastically about the Dan Flavin installation. The Subramaniam family established a small donor-advised fund at Fidelity Charitable that channels giving to arts and education causes. Priya has the relationship and should schedule a private viewing of the upcoming Judd-related materials in the collection. Potential ask: $15,000 for the acquisition endowment.

attributes.content: Eduardo Villanueva-Rios spent fifteen years at Goldman Sachs in the Investment Banking Division, where he ultimately made managing director before leaving to co-found a boutique M&A advisory firm focused on Latin American media transactions. He lives in Tribeca with his wife and two teenage sons. Eduardo's collecting passion is Basquiat and the broader Neo-Expressionist circle — he owns a small Basquiat drawing acquired at Christie's in 2019 and has been building out related works by Keith Haring and Kerry James Marshall. He attended Art Basel Miami Beach every year for the past six years and describes the Untitled Art Fair there as equally important to his discovery process. He is a trustee of the Public Art Fund and helped underwrite a mural commission in the South Bronx two years ago. His family operates the Villanueva-Rios Cultural Foundation, which focuses on Latino arts organizations in New York. A major gift conversation at the $50,000 level is being planned for early 2027; relationship manager recommends the director make the ask personally over dinner.

Isabel Castillo-Vargas is a managing director at a technology-focused growth equity firm in Midtown, having joined from a product management role at a major fintech platform. She completed her MBA at Columbia Business School and grew up in Los Angeles, where her family is still based. Isabel lives in a high-floor apartment in Midtown with views of the Hudson. Her collecting interest is contemporary figurative painting — she discovered Eric Fischl through a museum exhibition three years ago and has since acquired two of his works. She has been tracking Jenny Saville and Nicole Eisenman closely and attended Art Basel Miami Beach last December specifically to explore figurative work. She participates in a women's triathlon group and completed Ironman Lake Placid last August. She is a junior member of the Public Art Fund's associates circle and has expressed interest in growing her museum involvement alongside her philanthropic profile more broadly. Annual fund ask of $4,500, with a note to consider her for the Young Leaders Council forming in 2027.

Jasmine Oduya is a managing director in Goldman Sachs's consumer and healthcare investment banking group. She grew up in Lagos, Nigeria, moved to London for university, and came to New York for her MBA at Columbia. She has been at Goldman for eight years and lives in a sleek apartment in the Financial District. Jasmine's collecting interests bridge contemporary African art and international photography — she owns works by Zanele Muholi and has been in active discussions about acquiring a large-format Taryn Simon photograph. She attended Frieze London every October and attended Frieze New York for the first time this past May. She is on the emerging leaders council of the Brooklyn Museum and attended their trustee dinner last year. Jasmine completed the Chicago Marathon last October, her first marathon, and is already registered for New York next November. She is 33 and still in the early arc of her philanthropic development, but her income trajectory and cultural commitments make her a priority cultivation target. Annual fund ask of $3,500, with a mid-level upgrade path over the next two cycles.

Marcus Webb is a managing director in equity research at Goldman Sachs, covering the luxury goods and consumer discretionary sectors. His professional focus on the luxury market bleeds into his personal life — he collects design objects and has recently begun acquiring figurative paintings, particularly works by Jenny Saville and Lucian Freud. He attended Art Basel Basel last year for the first time as a buyer rather than a browser and was struck by the institutional quality of the fair's main sector. Marcus lives in a renovated townhouse in Carroll Gardens with his partner and their dog. He has been a museum member for three years and attended two evening events, including the Freud lecture series co-presented with the Freud Museum London. Michael Torres manages the relationship. Marcus is a USTA club tennis player and competes in weekend ladder matches at a Cobble Hill sports club. He has expressed interest in the museum's corporate membership program as a vehicle for client entertainment and museum access. Next step: introduce him to the corporate partnerships team and explore a Director's Circle upgrade at $15,000. His research platform also offers potential for a sponsored content partnership around the museum's design programming.

Rodrigo Esparza is a managing director in Goldman Sachs's investment banking division, focused on Latin American cross-border transactions. He joined the bank in 2003 after completing his MBA at Wharton and previously worked at Citigroup's capital markets group in Mexico City. Rodrigo and his wife Carmen live in Tribeca with their teenage daughter. His collecting interests center on Basquiat and Neo-Expressionism broadly — he owns two early Haring works and has been building toward a Kerry James Marshall acquisition. He attended the museum's gala in November and the Neo-Expressionism panel discussion in March, where he spoke briefly with the director. Rodrigo is also a board member of the Public Art Fund and has been supportive of its street-level installation programming. He skis regularly at Verbier each January. Cultivation notes: James Reuter is the relationship manager. Rodrigo's last gift was $10,000 at the major donor level. Given his board engagement at Public Art Fund and alignment with our programming, James believes a $25,000 ask is appropriate at the next cycle. Initial conversation should happen at the fall preview dinner.

Richard Nakagawa is a managing director at a private equity firm focused on healthcare services buyouts, having previously spent eight years at Goldman Sachs's financial sponsors group in the healthcare vertical. Richard was born in Los Angeles, where his family has lived for three generations, and recently relocated with his wife and two children to Greenwich, Connecticut, though he maintains strong New York ties. His collecting focuses on figurative painting — he has been building a focused collection around Eric Fischl's beach and domestic scene paintings and recently acquired a mid-period canvas through a dealer in Chelsea. Richard attended Art Basel Basel last June and Art Basel Miami in December, and described his Basel trip as the most productive three days he has spent in the art world. He was introduced to the museum by a Goldman alumni colleague and made his first gift of $8,000 last spring. Cultivation notes: Sarah Okafor manages the account. Richard is a strong new relationship with Goldman alumni overlap with several other donors. His Fischl focus aligns with upcoming figurative painting programming. Sarah recommends a curator meeting and a $15,000 ask for year two.

Vikram Nair is a managing director in Goldman Sachs's investment banking division, where he has worked for eleven years following a prior stint at JPMorgan Chase. He focuses primarily on technology M&A and has a particular interest in media sector transactions. Vikram began attending museum preview evenings in 2021 through a colleague referral and has since come to three curator-led gallery walkthroughs. He responded strongly to the museum's Franz Kline retrospective, citing a long-standing passion for Abstract Expressionism — he currently holds works by Kline and Lee Krasner acquired through Sotheby's and a private dealer in London. He and his wife Ananya live on the Upper East Side with their two school-age children. Outside of work Vikram races with a Swan 48 he co-owns called Breakwater in the Newport-Bermuda race; next year's campaign is already planned. He supports the Guggenheim Foundation as an annual donor. Cultivation note: Priya Mehta should schedule a studio visit before year-end; a mid-level ask in the $25K range is appropriate to test ceiling.

attributes.content: Nadia Rousseau is a deputy chief investment officer at a major university endowment, where she oversees real assets and alternative credit allocations. She previously worked at a sovereign wealth fund in Abu Dhabi and before that at Goldman Sachs's asset management division in New York and London. She holds a master's degree in finance from the London School of Economics. She and her partner live in Harlem and have recently become involved in arts initiatives in that community. Nadia has been a museum member for three years and attends consistently. Her collecting interests center on Minimalism and she has acquired two pieces through museum benefit auctions — an Anne Truitt work on paper and a Dan Flavin photographic documentation print. She attended Art Basel Miami Beach this year. She gives to the Harlem Stage arts organization and is considering board candidacy. Diana Flores manages the relationship. Nadia is a dedicated road cyclist and completed the Étape du Tour amateur stage race in France this summer. A mid-tier cultivation path is appropriate — a $10,000 ask tied to the Minimalism collection care fund is the planned approach.

Aleksei Volkov is a managing director in Goldman Sachs's wealth management division, serving ultra-high-net-worth families with ties to Eastern Europe and Russia. He was born in St. Petersburg, immigrated to the United States at age sixteen, and studied economics and art history at Yale before joining Goldman. He lives in Midtown East and collects primarily postwar European painting and Abstract Expressionism — he owns a de Kooning drawing and a Rothko work on paper, and has expressed interest in adding a major Pollock to the collection. He attended Art Basel Basel this past June and spent considerable time at the Hauser & Wirth booth. Aleksei is fluent in Russian, German, and English and has facilitated introductions between the museum and several Eastern European private lenders. He donates to the Yale Art Gallery and to a foundation supporting classical music education in Ukraine. Cultivation note: James Reuter to explore loan opportunities as a cultivation step before any direct ask; Aleksei responds well to curatorial engagement. Capacity: $30,000–$75,000.

Andre Beaumont is a forty-year-old partner at a Bain Capital-affiliated real estate investment platform based in Boston, though he has lived in the West Village for five years after relocating for personal reasons. He attended Williams College and Harvard Business School, with a summer in the Bain consulting program between degrees. His collecting interests focus on contemporary figurative painting — he owns works by Nicole Eisenman and Eric Fischl, and is on the waitlist for a Jenny Saville studio visit. He attended Frieze New York in May and Frieze London in October as part of a self-described annual art circuit. He was introduced to the museum at an Art Leaders evening in early spring and made his first gift within a week of the event. He also skis at Aspen each winter, typically for two weeks, and is part of a group that books a house on Red Mountain. Cultivation note: Diana Flores to build on the momentum from his initial gift; Andre is responsive and moves quickly when engaged. A mid-level ask of $5,000 is well within range for this fiscal year.

Omar Shaikh is a forty-four-year-old managing director in Goldman Sachs's equity capital markets division, covering technology sector IPOs and follow-on offerings. He grew up in Pakistan, attended the London School of Economics, and completed his MBA at Chicago Booth before joining Goldman. He lives in a modern apartment in Tribeca with his wife and two young children. His collecting interests are in contemporary photography and design: he owns prints by Wolfgang Tillmans and Taryn Simon and recently acquired a design piece from Galerie kreo in Paris. He attended Art Basel Basel and Frieze London last year. He supports several Pakistani education nonprofits through the Shaikh Family Trust and is an advisory board member of the Aga Khan Museum in Toronto. Cultivation note: Michael Torres to explore an alignment between the museum's Islamic art holdings and Omar's Pakistani cultural identity; this has not yet been raised in cultivation conversations and could deepen personal resonance. Mid-level ask of $10,000 appropriate given his financial profile. Handle with care around his travel schedule.

Tariq Al-Rashid is an investment banker at a boutique restructuring advisory firm in Midtown, having spent his earlier career at Goldman Sachs in the Leveraged Finance group. He holds an MBA from Booth and a bachelor's from Georgetown. Tariq lives in Park Slope with his wife Leila and their three children. His collecting interests are in figurative painting — he is particularly drawn to Lucian Freud and Jenny Saville and attended a lecture at the museum on contemporary British figuration that he described as 'genuinely revelatory.' He has attended Art Basel Miami the past three years, usually with a group of collector friends from the finance world. Tariq is a devoted skier who spends a week each February at Zermatt; his children take lessons while he skis off-piste. Michael Torres introduced him to the museum through a peer referral and has cultivated the relationship over two years. Current giving is at the Patron level. An ask in the $20,000–$30,000 range for a dedicated education program fund is planned for the first quarter of next year.

Raymond Osei is a 49-year-old managing director at JPMorgan Asset Management, overseeing a multi-strategy institutional portfolio. He spent four years at Goldman Sachs in equity research before joining JPMorgan. Raymond lives in Scarsdale and commutes daily. He and his wife Abena are enthusiastic patrons of the arts. Raymond collects works by Basquiat-era artists and Kerry James Marshall — he attended the museum's Marshall retrospective lecture and requested a private follow-up viewing of the museum's Marshall holdings, which took place last fall. He is a board member of the Studio Museum in Harlem. Raymond supports the museum at the mid-tier level and has given consistently for six years. Michael Torres manages the relationship. Cultivation note: Raymond's dual board engagement (Studio Museum and active here) creates a natural bridge for a leadership gift conversation — a trustee nomination should be explored in parallel with an upgrade ask at the $75,000 level. He is analytical and responds best to data-supported impact narratives.
